name: OH-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 21 points on the partisan baseline
Jordan's fundraising dominance: $5.5 million raised and $4.6 million on hand versus roughly $25,000 for the Democrat
High-profile incumbent seeking re-election with no ratings or polls showing a competitive race
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 95%
model.rationale: The seat sits in a district that favors Republicans by about 21 points, Jordan holds a roughly 200-to-1 fundraising advantage, and prediction markets price his odds near 95%, with no polling or expert ratings suggesting competitiveness.
model.watch: A large national wave toward Democrats could narrow the margin, but flipping the seat would require a shift far beyond anything recent Ohio polling implies.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Jordan, a high-profile Republican incumbent, seeks re-election in a west-central Ohio district that leans Republican by about 21 points at the presidential level. He has raised more than $5.5 million and holds $4.6 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Joshua Kolasinski has reported minimal fundraising. No public polls of the race are available, and no national race raters have flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets give Jordan roughly a 95 percent chance of winning.

The structural picture strongly favors the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, Jordan's name recognition from his national profile, and the enormous fundraising gap leave the Democrat with little visible path. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but reports no campaign activity. The expected margin sits near 19 points Republican, with residual uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling.
